name: unification

phase_0.boundary_condition: The symmetric informationally complete positive operator-valued measure frame that contains all theorem coordinates and their transitions.

⊢.justification: The void state before any theorem is interrogated or any measurement is defined.

⊣.justification: The closed boundary containing the universal frame against which all operator-valued measures are defined.

≻.justification: The directed morphism moving a problem from its open state toward a settled classification.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism where a diverging correlation length collapses into a gapped state or vice versa.

⋈.justification: The sequential chaining of the twelve coordinates that define a specific theorem object.

⊙.justification: The state where the theorem recognizes itself as a measurement, distinct from its proof.

∈.justification: The split into the affirmative arm (positive winding) and the negative arm (integer winding count).

∋.justification: The fusion of the winding arms into a single B4 verdict, often B when positivity and negativity coexist.

⊤.justification: The affirmative state where the winding is 0 or 1/2, corresponding to a positive measure.

⊥.justification: The negative state where the winding is an integer n, corresponding to a non-positive measure.

⊞.justification: The state where a non-commuting state is held simultaneously by every observer, a contradiction kept live.

◻.justification: The permanent, append-only record of a theorem's classification once it has been settled.

phase_2.fuse_result: A single B4 verdict representing the theorem's classification

phase_3.void_description: The state before any theorem is defined or any measurement is taken.
phase_3.true_description: A theorem with a self-inverse winding (0 or 1/2), representing a positive operator-valued measure.
phase_3.false_description: A theorem with an integer winding count, representing a non-positive operator-valued measure.
phase_3.both_description: A theorem where the broadcast coordinate holds a non-commuting state simultaneously for all observers, a paradice of contradiction.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the coordinate space for the unification of theorems.
Anchor the system within the universal symmetric informationally complete frame.
Branch the measurement into the positive (self-inverse) and negative (integer) winding arms.
Move along the positive arm toward the self-inverse winding state.
Affirm the self-inverse winding as the positive measure.
Reverse along the negative arm toward the integer winding count.
Affirm the integer winding as the negative measure.
Fuse the positive and negative arms into a single B4 verdict.
Compose the twelve coordinates of the theorem object.
Establish the self-referential identity of the theorem as a measurement.
Hold the broadcast coordinate where a non-commuting state is shared by all observers.
Record the settled classification of the theorem as a permanent fact.
Chain the transition from the open question to the settled theorem.
Advance the criticality coordinate from diverging to gapped.
Reverse the criticality coordinate from gapped to diverging.
Fuse the criticality arms into a single verdict on global regularity.
Fix the final classification of the theorem in the settled state.
Close the system within the reference frame.

phase_6.post_cycle_state: The settled theorem state concentrated in the complete, negative, static cell.

∈=𐑔: Unification implies a global integration where interactions propagate across the entire system to merge distinct parts into a single coherent whole.
